<h1 align="center" border="none">eleventy-plugin-netlify-data-store</h1>

<p align="center">

<p align="center"><b>Read & write build-time content for Eleventy from Netlify Blobs, with a TTL-based local cache for fast, offline-tolerant builds.</b></p>

## Overview

Content lives in a Netlify Blobs store — written by whatever writes it: a
scheduled function, a form handler, a webhook — & is read at build time through
a local cache that keeps builds fast & survives a bad network.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Source of truth | A Netlify Blobs store |
| Read path | The local cache while the entry is inside its TTL, otherwise the store |
| After a fetch | The result is cached, so the next build can run offline |
| If the store is unreachable | An expired entry is served with `meta.stale` set |

The plugin never reads Eleventy's data directory. Anything you want in git
belongs in `_data/`, which Eleventy already loads on its own.

Every stored value uses a `{ meta, ...content }` envelope, & every read returns
that whole envelope, so a template destructures metadata & content together:

```njk
{% if activity.meta.error %}
  <p>Activity unavailable.</p>
{% else %}
  <p>Updated {{ activity.meta.generatedAt | generatedAt }}</p>
  {% if activity.meta.stale %}<p>Showing the last cached copy.</p>{% endif %}
{% endif %}
```

Reads & writes never throw. A read that fails resolves to
`{ meta: { name, store, source, error } }`; a write resolves to
`{ statusCode, body }`. A template renders a fallback instead of failing the
build.

## Installation

```bash
yarn add @allons-y/eleventy-plugin-netlify-data-store
```

Requires Node 22.12+ & Eleventy 3.0+.

## Usage

```js
// eleventy.config.js
import netlifyDataStore from "@allons-y/eleventy-plugin-netlify-data-store";

export default function (eleventyConfig) {
	let { readBlob, listData } = eleventyConfig.addPlugin(netlifyDataStore, {
		immediate: true,
		storeName: "content",
		ttl: "1h",
	});

	eleventyConfig.addGlobalData("activity", () => readBlob("activity"));
}
```

`immediate: true` runs the plugin during the config file rather than after it,
which is what makes the destructuring above work. Without it, reach for
`eleventyConfig.netlifyDataStore` from inside a callback, where the plugin has
already run:

```js
eleventyConfig.addPlugin(netlifyDataStore, { ttl: "1h" });

eleventyConfig.addGlobalData("activity", () =>
	eleventyConfig.netlifyDataStore.readBlob("activity")
);
```

Outside Eleventy — in a scheduled function, say — build a store directly:

```js
import { createDataStore } from "@allons-y/eleventy-plugin-netlify-data-store";

const { writeBlob } = createDataStore({ storeName: "content" });

export default async () =>
	writeBlob("activity", {
		meta: { generatedAt: new Date().toISOString() },
		entries: await fetchEntries(),
	});
```

### Credentials

`NETLIFY_SITE_ID` & `NETLIFY_TOKEN` must be set for any read or write that
reaches Netlify Blobs. Missing credentials are a configuration error:
`getStore` throws, & the calling `readBlob`/`writeBlob` converts that into the
usual envelope or `{ statusCode: 500 }` so the build still completes. The
reason is always logged.

A read served from a warm cache needs no credentials at all — which is what
lets a build run offline.

## API

| Function | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `readBlob(name, storeName?)` | The full `{ meta, ...content }` envelope, or `{ meta: { error } }` |
| `writeBlob(name, data, storeName?)` | `{ statusCode, body }` |
| `listData(storeName?)` | `string[]` of blob keys — the local cache's keys in development |
| `formatGeneratedAt(value)` | A formatted `meta.generatedAt`, or `""` when missing or unparseable |

`readBlob` resolves in this order:

1. **The local cache**, when the entry exists & is younger than `ttl`.
2. **Netlify Blobs** otherwise — & the result is written into the cache.
3. **The stale cache**, if the store could not be reached & `staleIfError` is
   on. The envelope comes back with `meta.stale` & `meta.cacheAge` added, and
   the original `meta.generatedAt` intact.

`writeBlob` writes to the store & refreshes the cached copy, so a read that
follows it sees the new value immediately.

## Options

```js
eleventyConfig.addPlugin(netlifyDataStore, {
	storeName: "content",          // default Netlify Blobs store
	cacheDir: ".netlify/blobs-cache", // local, uncommitted cache
	ttl: "1h",                     // how long a cached entry stays fresh
	staleIfError: true,            // serve an expired entry if the store is unreachable
	siteID: undefined,             // defaults to process.env.NETLIFY_SITE_ID
	token: undefined,              // defaults to process.env.NETLIFY_TOKEN
	quiet: false,                  // suppress per-read logging (errors still log)
	locale: "en-GB",               // for formatGeneratedAt
	dateFormat: undefined,         // Intl.DateTimeFormat options for formatGeneratedAt
	filterName: "generatedAt",     // filter to register; false to skip
	getStore: undefined,           // advanced: supply your own store factory
});
```

### `ttl`

Accepts the same duration strings as `eleventy-fetch` — `"30s"`, `"30m"`,
`"1h"`, `"7d"`, `"2w"`, `"1y"` — plus `"*"` to never expire & `0` to refetch on
every build. A raw number is milliseconds. An unparseable value throws at
registration rather than mid-build.

The cache applies to every build, not just local development: CI & production
builds read it too, which cuts Blobs calls & build time. `NODE_ENV` plays no
part.

### `staleIfError`

On by default. When the entry has expired *and* the store cannot be reached —
an outage, a missing credential, a deleted blob — the expired copy is served
rather than failing, carrying `meta.stale: true` & `meta.cacheAge` in
milliseconds so a template can say how old it is. Set it to `false` to never
serve data past its TTL; reads then return the usual error envelope.

### The local cache

`cacheDir` holds a mirror of the store at
`<cacheDir>/<storeName>/<name>.json`. Each file wraps the value with the time
it was fetched:

```json
{
	"cachedAt": "2026-09-05T06:15:00.000Z",
	"value": { "meta": { "generatedAt": "…" }, "entries": [] }
}
```

It is a cache, not a fixture: written by the plugin, never committed, & safe to
delete. Add it to `.gitignore`:

```gitignore
.netlify
```

Warming it takes one build with credentials present; every build after that
runs offline until the TTL lapses.

## Sample

`sample/` is a minimal Eleventy site that reads entirely from the cache, with
no network access & no credentials. It points `cacheDir` at a committed fixture
& pins `ttl: "*"` so the fixture never expires:

```bash
yarn sample
```

## Testing

```bash
yarn test    # ava
yarn lint
```

Netlify Blobs is never contacted: tests pass a fake store factory through the
`getStore` option.

## Releasing with changesets

Releases are managed by [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets).
When you make a change that affects how the plugin behaves for consumers, add a
changeset:

```bash
yarn changeset
```

Pick the bump type when prompted, write a short but descriptive summary, & commit
the generated file in `.changeset/` alongside your code:

- **patch** — bug fixes
- **minor** — new, backwards-compatible features
- **major** — breaking changes

On every push to `main` the Release workflow opens or updates a **"Version
packages"** PR; merging it publishes to npm & tags the release. Don't edit
`version` in `package.json` or the released sections of `CHANGELOG.md` by hand.

Please be sure that changes are written for a human reader rather than a short
commit message. Changes that don't affect consumers (docs, tests, CI, internal
refactors) don't need a changeset.

Full details are in [CONTRIBUTING.md](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).
